name: Hydrocotyle
look_here_first: Inspect the entire flowering stalk. H. umbellata generally has a dense terminal many-flowered cluster; H. verticillata has several spaced whorls along an elongate axis.
shared_traits: Creeping wetland herbs rooting at nodes, with round peltate leaves.
Small flowers and flattened two-part ribbed fruits.

comparison_matrix.umbellata: Usually a dense terminal cluster; may produce a few extra tiers.
comparison_matrix.verticillata: Multiple distinct whorls separated along an elongated axis.

comparison_matrix.umbellata: Often 15–35 or more flowers in the dense terminal cluster.
comparison_matrix.verticillata: Often 4–8 flowers per whorl in the local var. triradiata treatment.

comparison_matrix.umbellata: Flattened, two-mericarps; base sometimes distinctly notched.
comparison_matrix.verticillata: Flattened, two-mericarps; base sometimes more rounded.

overlap_cautions: Umbellata may produce additional whorls; inspect the whole axis.
Crowded upper whorls of verticillata may appear as a single cluster.
Use fruit only as supporting evidence; leaves alone do not distinguish the species.
Precise verticillata measurements from UT Austin refer to var. triradiata.

lookalikes.separator: Petiole joins the leaf at the basal notch, rather than centrally.
Leaves are basally attached rather than peltate.

diagnostic_photo_checklist: Matched full flowering stalks showing number and spacing of whorls, with millimeter scale.
Matched close-ups counting flowers in each tier.
Leaf undersides showing peltate petiole attachment and rooting nodes.
Mature fruits with base shape, ribs and scale.
handoffs: Diagnostic Photo Polish: acquire matched flowering-axis macros.
Approved Taxa Installer: neither source-pool species currently canonical.
Taxonomy + Diagnostic Review: verify ambiguous few-whorled specimens and infraspecific concepts.
